title: Caesar
publisher: Self-published (Impressions Games); Sierra On-Line acquired the studio in 1995
engineNote: Top-down, pre-isometric — predates the shared SG/.555 pipeline entirely. Its own reverse-engineering problem, not a variant of the others. Amiga first (Oct 12, 1992), DOS/Atari ST/Mac in 1993.
timelineNote: Top-down, pre-isometric — predates the shared SG/.555 pipeline entirely, its own reverse-engineering problem. Designer David Lester, programmer Simon Bradbury. Amiga first (Oct 12), DOS/Atari ST/Mac in 1993.
wanted: No open-source engine or format documentation exists for Caesar — completely virgin reverse-engineering territory.

title: Caesar II
credits: David Lester (design) · Simon Bradbury (programming) · Chris Beatrice (art)
engineNote: Transitional generation between Caesar and Caesar III — still no open documentation of its asset formats.
timelineNote: Transitional generation. Same core team (Lester/Bradbury), Chris Beatrice joining on art. Still no open documentation of its asset formats.
wanted: No open-source engine or format documentation exists for Caesar II either.

title: Caesar III
engineNote: The archetype. Isometric 2D sprites on .sg2 + .555 assets, .map scenarios, .sav saves. The official map editor landed in the v1.1 patch — the engine every later title in this era shares.
timelineNote: Isometric 2D sprites on the .sg2 + .555 asset pipeline, .map scenarios, .sav saves. Official map editor landed in the v1.1 patch.

title: Pharaoh
engineNote: Same engine as Caesar III, moved to Egypt and onto .sg3.
timelineNote: Same engine as Caesar III, moved to Ancient Egypt, now on .sg3. Bundled as Pharaoh Gold in 2001.

title: Zeus: Master of Olympus
engineNote: An engine revamp, not a reskin: global labor pool replaces labor walkers, no forts, elite housing built directly.
timelineNote: An engine revamp: global labor pool replaces labor walkers, no forts, elite housing built directly. Same designer/programmer team as Pharaoh.

title: Emperor: Rise of the Middle Kingdom
setting: Ancient China, Xia → Song-Jin (2033 BC–1234 AD)
engineNote: Built on the Zeus engine. Last title on the 2D sprite engine, and the first in the series with multiplayer.
timelineNote: Built on the Zeus engine, spanning Xia to Song-Jin China. Last title on the 2D sprite engine, and the first with multiplayer.
wanted: No open-source engine reimplementation exists for Emperor — confirmed across two research passes. It shares the Zeus engine generation and .sg3/.555 formats, so an eZeus- or Julius-lineage fork is technically plausible. The most credible open target in the whole archive.
